title: Malformed bracket order panics instead of returning compile error
evidence: NIG finds '[' and ']' independently then slices line[start..=end] without checking start <= end; DAH and LAL repeat it.
trigger: Compile NIG X ] [ Y (three or more tokens).
impact: Rust string slicing panics at an invalid range, aborting compilation rather than returning Result::Err.

title: Named registers silently alias after six variables
evidence: next_idx = 2 + ((sym_table.len() as u8) % 6) assigns the seventh distinct symbol register 2 again. VM LoadReg writes that physical register (vm.rs:283-290).
trigger: Compile a script with seven distinct symbolic destinations.
impact: Writing the seventh variable corrupts the first variable; compilation succeeds without exhausting-register diagnostic.

title: NIG silently truncates multi-place literals to 255
evidence: parse_cuneiform_literal returns u64 but NIG/DAH/LAL lower val.min(255) to a single byte instead of rejecting or representing the value. VM SexaPack reads one byte of seconds (vm.rs:270-278).
trigger: Compile NIG X [ Y - - ], a sexagesimal literal equal to 3600.
impact: The accepted program stores 255 instead of 3600 with no diagnostic.

title: Closed completion channel causes an infinite busy loop after consensus timeout
evidence: Orchestrator exits on its 15-second timeout at lines 228–232, dropping tx_completed; receive loop at 306–346 handles only Some and never None. BftSwarmEngine::run_dag calls this engine on a current-thread Tokio runtime (bindings.rs:368–380).
trigger: A nonempty DAG fails to complete within 15 seconds, including concurrency_limit=0 or unavailable quorum.
impact: recv immediately returns None forever; request never returns, rollback and worker-stop code remain unreachable, and the async thread spins.

title: Database errors leave committed in-memory DAG changes despite rollback error
evidence: Memory is mutated at 335; snapshot restoration occurs only for node failure and score failure. Database open/pragma/insert/commit errors at 384–408 return through ? without restoring snapshot. bindings.rs reports every Err as BFT Rollback Triggered.
trigger: A DAG passes node and score checks, then SQLite open, insert, or commit fails.
impact: Caller receives an error claiming rollback while shared memory retains the DAG changes and durable state does not reflect them.

title: Lifecycle validation never verifies the certificate signature
evidence: Docstring at 422 promises expiration, revocation and signature verification. Implementation only checks CRL membership and valid_until, then returns valid=True at 460-464 without calling verify_certificate_signature.
trigger: Pass a fabricated unsigned certificate with a future valid_until and no matching CRL entry to verify_certificate_lifecycle.
impact: Caller receives ACTIVE/valid=True for an unauthenticated or modified certificate.

title: Decision evidence packet does not bind decision data to the proved ledger event
evidence: Lines 473-479 obtain ledger integrity/root/proof for seq; line 488 independently includes caller-supplied decision_data, with no lookup or comparison. CortexPersistLedger.get_event_proof (592-608) returns only an entry-hash inclusion proof. Existing test at tests/test_compliance_exporter.py:149 supplies loan data unrelated to the stored action_id payload.
trigger: Create a packet for a valid ledger seq while supplying decision_data describing a different action.
impact: Signed packet presents unrelated decision data alongside a valid inclusion proof; third parties cannot establish that the claimed decision was logged from this packet.

title: Recovery proposals execute without Trust Gateway reevaluation
evidence: execute_step evaluates original proposal at 208-213, but recovery_fixer returns a new proposal at 304 and sandbox_runner(fixed_proposal) runs at 311 without evaluate or replay check.
trigger: An admitted action fails and recovery_fixer changes the target to a sensitive path, tool, or previously failed action.
impact: The callback receives the changed action without the deterministic rejection applied to normal actions; record_step_atomic then records ADMIT if it succeeds. Scope is this executor callback boundary, not proof of an OS sandbox escape.

title: Required structured review is only a quota counter
evidence: Lines 255-258 spend recovery quota and set structured_review_used=True; line 260 unconditionally calls sandbox_runner. No review callable, review output, or approval decision exists.
trigger: An irreversible/architectural proposal requires review, including when recovery quota is exhausted.
impact: The action executes without the required independent review, and successful events may report structured_review=True despite no review being performed.

title: Legion PoC passes without asserting any receipt was persisted
evidence: SQLite count is read and printed at 242–245; the sole final assertion checks receipts_generated >= 1, counting enqueue attempts.
trigger: Receipts are generated but the asynchronous ledger stores zero rows without surfacing an exception here.
impact: PoC reports success despite failing its stated acceptance criterion of at least one inserted receipt.

title: Legion PoC claims validation of 1000 agents from a sequential batch of 100 advisories
evidence: batch = all_advisories[:100] at 153; three processors run sequentially; final success line claims topology validated for 1000 agents.
trigger: A normal successful execution of this demonstration.
impact: Output overstates the exercised scale and concurrency; it provides no 1000-agent runtime evidence.

title: Multi-tenant example trusts a caller-selected identity
evidence: userId comes directly from X-User-ID; getSession(userId) and createSession({id:userId}) use it within the shared multi-tenant sandbox (170-181).
trigger: Deploy the documented handler where different callers can set X-User-ID and request another caller's session ID.
impact: The example supplies no authentication binding, allowing session selection across tenants if adopted directly; this is an example defect, not evidence of a deployed service.

title: CI example interpolates request JSON into a shell command
evidence: repo and branch are read from request.json at 135 and directly interpolated into sandbox.exec git clone at 138.
trigger: Adopt the example and submit shell metacharacters through repo or branch.
impact: Input changes the command structure and can execute unintended shell commands inside the CI sandbox; no host escape is claimed.

title: TLA liveness comments claim a physical deadline absent from the model
evidence: Spec uses weak fairness and Termination is eventual state completion; no clock, deadline, bounded delay, or physical-time constant is modeled.
trigger: Readers use the advertised termination in T seconds or absence of network deadlocks as an operational guarantee.
impact: Unbounded eventual progress under assumed fairness is presented as bounded physical termination, overstating the proof scope.

title: Tokenizer cannot encode ordinary Unicode outside Latin-1
evidence: The initial vocabulary contains chr(0)..chr(255), but encode splits Unicode text into characters and directly indexes self.vocab at line 85. Training adds merged strings only, never missing singleton characters.
trigger: Encode an unseen character such as U+20AC or a CJK character; a single-character training input also adds nothing.
impact: The text-to-token API raises KeyError for valid multilingual input instead of representing UTF-8 bytes or unknown tokens.

title: Exported MemoryStore silently drops all writes
evidence: MemoryStore.set is pass (lines 47-48); get unconditionally returns None (44-45). The class is exported in __all__. Targeted search found no current internal caller.
trigger: A consumer imports the public MemoryStore API, calls set and subsequently get.
impact: The write reports no failure and data cannot be retrieved; the public persistence-looking API cannot preserve state. No active internal data-loss path is claimed.

title: Rule evaluation reports SAT when a required property is absent
evidence: Violation creation is inside if let Some(val); missing properties have no branch. Line78 sets SAT whenever violations is empty. main.rs131 consumes this result and132 derives has_violations solely from the empty list.
trigger: Evaluate a matching IFC entity without the rule.target property.
impact: A model with no evidence for the regulated dimension receives SAT and no violation; deleting the numeric property can turn a failing check into a passing report.

title: Thermal budget addition can overflow before admission comparison
evidence: current + cost is used in both comparison and CAS without checked addition.
trigger: After one admitted unit, public try_admit(usize::MAX) overflows.
impact: Debug builds panic; ordinary release overflow can wrap to a small value and admit a cost exceeding max_heat. No external caller for this cost found in src/crates.

title: Byte-sized fields are emitted as eight-byte stores
evidence: Layout assigns Bool size/alignment (1,1) at 85, but Store/VolatileStore always emit mov qword [rax],rcx at 193–198; Load also uses qword.
trigger: Use the public layout/backend path for a struct containing two Bool fields; its allocation is two bytes.
impact: Generated assembly writes eight bytes for each Bool field, overwriting neighbors and allocated bounds. Existing Sensor example hides this by putting Bool in tail padding.

title: Benchmark conclusions attribute simulator assumptions to external products
evidence: Disseqt simulator explicitly sleeps 5ms per batch (57,77); C5 branch uses Python Lock and bytearray (130–146). Lines 235–238 present measured simulator ratio and assumed cost/queue arithmetic as statements about Disseqt, KLA/SupraWall and AgentAudit, without running their implementations.
trigger: Run comparative demonstration and reuse printed conclusions.
impact: Output cannot support product performance, evidence-preservation or fleet-freeze claims; it measures the chosen simulation and unrelated work rather than equivalent product behavior.

title: SRP falsification compares predetermined conflict models and unequal workloads
evidence: A counts actor switches on consecutive changes; B/C retain each file owner forever at lines 224-237 rather than the claimed two-change window. C has disjoint assigned file lists so zero cross-actor conflicts follows from input construction. In the timing loop A appends every digest to audit_log (line 61), whereas B and C do not persist records. Lines 323-332 print unconditional architecture conclusions.
trigger: Run the purported empirical falsification report to compare architecture conflicts or dispatch latency.
impact: Its conflict totals have different denominators/history and its timings include unequal persistence work, so the report cannot support the stated comparative conclusions.

title: Cancer pipeline emits attested numerical invariants without inputs or computation
evidence: run_cancer_isomorphism_pipeline constructs fixed morphism_preservation=True, spectral_radius_bound=0.021, isomorphism_degree=1:1_DETERMINISTIC and status=ATTESTED at 18-28. CLI accepts only --json.
trigger: Any invocation, including with no cellular model or observations available.
impact: Machine consumers receive fabricated verification status and a numerical bound presented as pipeline results; this supplies no scientific evidence for the asserted invariants.

title: Installer commits unrelated staged changes and hides copy failures
evidence: Every cp is suppressed with || true; git commit has no pathspec and the script has no fail-fast handling.
trigger: Run installer in a repository with unrelated staged changes or with missing source assets.
impact: Existing staged work can be included in its generated commit; failed installation still prints READY.

title: Python SharedManifest example uses an incompatible ABI
evidence: Example fields begin with session_id[16], domain_mask and effect_class; src/manifest.rs tests require status_flag at 0, seq at 4, epoch_id at 8, payload_hash at 16. Only sizeof is checked at 30.
trigger: Use this advertised FFI structure to interpret the repository SharedManifest.
impact: Fields read unrelated bytes; a 64-byte size check falsely claims alignment and ABI equivalence. Local demo allocates its own buffer, so no actual shared-memory corruption is established.

title: Synthetic worker scores are presented without a simulation label
evidence: agent_worker only sleeps and derives exergy = 15000.0 + (agent_idx * 17.3) % 6000.0; it then emits verdicts including FALSACIÓN_POPPERIANA and cohort names for hardware/SEP/SMT topics. No corresponding checks occur in this file.
trigger: Running this script and interpreting its JSON cohort_stats/apex_agents as audit evidence.
impact: The output ranks fabricated arithmetic scores as audit verdicts without declaring a simulation, so it cannot support the hardware or security topics it names.

title: Syntax integrity gate omits the primary babylon60 package
evidence: TRACKED_DIRS lists root directories cli/core/etc but omits 01_KISH_ENGINE; enumeration at 23-30 scans only those roots and root-level Python files. Assigned runtime modules live in 01_KISH_ENGINE/babylon60/.
trigger: A SyntaxError is introduced into 01_KISH_ENGINE/babylon60 while this test is used as the advertised every-tracked-module syntax gate.
impact: The advertised structural gate never compiles the primary package and can pass despite syntax errors there.

title: Bearer-prefix example accepts arbitrary credentials
evidence: The complete Auth example at 148-150 only checks startsWith("Bearer "); no token comparison, signature verification, issuer, audience or expiry check follows before execution proceeds.
trigger: Copy the Security & Rate Limiting authentication example and send Authorization: Bearer arbitrary.
impact: Any caller can pass the illustrated authentication check and reach subsequent request handling.

title: Acoustic true-peak output measures only the mono sample peak
evidence: mono is 0.5*(left+right), then TruePeak_dBFS is computed from max(abs(mono)); no reconstruction or channel peak is evaluated.
trigger: Stereo channels are opposite in phase, or reconstructed intersample peaks exceed sample maxima.
impact: The reported TruePeak_dBFS can substantially underreport channel peak level and does not measure true peak.

title: Release attestor emits unsupported certification claims
evidence: Builder hardware/entropy_source and zero_leakage_certified=true, slsa_level=SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_3 are constants at 84–91; receipt at 102–106 contains only digest and statement, no signature or verification.
trigger: Run the script on any checkout/host and publish the emitted receipt.
impact: Artifact claims hardware and security provenance that the script never observes or verifies. No downstream acceptance/bypass was established.
